3. This is a petition seeking quashing of Fir No. 407/2019 dated 06.09.2019 u/s 420 Ipc read with
Section 12 of Passport Act registered at Ps Igi Airport.

4. Mr. Addy, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, very fairly states that the issues raised in
the petition are questions of fact for which detailed evidence would be required.

5.  Today, he restricts his prayer only to the fact that since the petitioner is a permanent resident of West Bengal, he need not be required to appear in person till the proceedings are pending before ACMM.

7. Section 317 Cr.P.C. reads as under:
Rahim Khan vs State (Nct, Delhi) on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41354130/
1 "317. Provision for inquiries and trial being held in the absence of accused in certain cases- (1) At any stage of an inquiry or trial under this Code, if the Judge or Magistrate is satisfied, for reasons to be recorded, that the personal attendance of the accused before the Court is not necessary in the interests of justice, or that the accused persistently disturbs the proceedings in Court, the Judge or Magistrate may, if the accused is represented by a pleader, dispense with his attendance and proceed with such inquiry or trial in his absence, and may, at any subsequent stage of the proceedings, direct the personal attendance of such accused.

(2) If the accused in any such case is not represented by a pleader, or if the Judge or Magistrate considers his personal attendance necessary, he may, if he thinks fit and for reasons to be recorded by him, either adjourn such inquiry or trial, or order that the case of such accused be taken up or tried separately."
8.

The Supreme Court in "Bhaskar Industries Ltd. vs. Bhiwani Denim & Apparels Ltd. & Ors."
[(2001) 7 SCC 401] while relying on Section 317 Cr.P.C. observed that if during a criminal proceeding, it appears to the Court that personal attendance may result in enormous hardship and cost to an accused, the Court may dispense with his personal attendance, after taking an undertaking from him that he would not dispute his identity as the particular accused in the case and that a counsel on his behalf would be present in Court.
9.
